name: Dual Littlestone Dimension
definition: For a finite binary class $\mathcal H$, let $\mathcal H^*=\{x^*:x\in\mathcal X\}$ be its dual class, where $x^*(h)=h(x)$ for $h\in\mathcal H$. The **dual Littlestone dimension** is $$\mathrm L^*(\mathcal H):=\mathrm L(\mathcal H^*).$$ Equivalently, it is the largest depth of a complete binary tree whose internal nodes are labeled by hypotheses of $\mathcal H$ and whose root-to-leaf label sequences are induced by coordinates of $\mathcal H$.
graph_summary: Littlestone dimension of the transposed incidence class: $\mathrm L^*(\mathcal H)=\mathrm L(\mathcal H^*)$.
description: The sequential/shattered-tree strengthening of dual VC dimension. It is standard in the private-learning literature; finite ordinary Littlestone dimension implies finite dual Littlestone dimension, albeit with a generally doubly exponential bound.

monotonic.proof: For $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal H$, the dual class $\mathcal G^*$ is obtained from $\mathcal H^*$ by restricting its domain to $\mathcal G$ and identifying duplicate functions. Projection monotonicity of Littlestone dimension gives $\mathrm L^*(\mathcal G)\le\mathrm L^*(\mathcal H)$.

p_monotonic.proof: The dual of a coordinate projection of $\mathcal H$ is a subfamily of $\mathcal H^*$, after duplicate projected concepts are identified. Subfamily monotonicity of Littlestone dimension gives the claim.

c_monotonic.proof: Conditioning is a subfamily restriction followed by a coordinate projection, so it follows from the preceding two properties.

doubly_monotonic.proof: The preceding subfamily- and projection-monotonicity arguments establish double monotonicity.
